authors: Xin Lu; Tianle Liu; Hanzhong Liu; Peng Ding
title: Design-based theory for cluster rerandomization
venue_or_arxiv: arXiv:2207.02540v1 (stat.ME); journal ref not shown on arXiv page [verify: recalled as Biometrika 2023, unconfirmed]
full_text_open: yes (arXiv); only abs page and part of the text read by summarizer
closeness: high for C5 (cluster-level Mahalanobis acceptance), but it is assignment of clusters to treatment, not sampling of clusters
what_it_holds: Cluster-randomized experiments with rerandomization on cluster-level covariates. Design-based, M clusters are a fixed finite population (no superpopulation sampling of clusters). HT and Hajek estimators of scaled cluster totals. Under Mahalanobis acceptance, the conditional limit is sqrt(1-R^2)*N(0,1) + R*(truncated normal L_{K,a}) with R^2 the squared multiple correlation between the estimator and its covariate-mean-difference (Li-Ding-Rubin form). Also compares weighted Euclidean vs Mahalanobis with covariate tiers, and recommends regression adjustment with robust SE. Closest published treatment of rejective acceptance at the cluster level; it gives the cluster analogue of the v_a variance factor for assignment, so the sampling analogue is not given here.

authors: Jason C. Legg; Cindy L. Yu
title: A comparison of sample set restriction procedures
venue_or_arxiv: Survey Methodology, issue 2010-01 (Statistics Canada cat. 12-001-X201000111249); pages [verify, not on catalogue page]
full_text_open: yes (Statcan open access); full PDF read via summariser
closeness: high for C5 vs C6 and for C7 (HT bias under rejection)
what_it_holds: Rejective sampling (Fuller 2009a): draw from an initial design (Poisson or stratified in the simulations), keep the sample if a quadratic distance between HT estimates of balancing variables and known means is below gamma (chi-square quantile), else redraw; proposes weighted rejection and two-step rejection to limit sample-size variation. Cube sampling via R sampling package, balancing on (p_i, x_i). Findings as summarised: regression estimators under cube and rejective have roughly equal efficiency; HT with the initial probabilities is unbiased under cube but BIASED under rejective because first-order inclusion probabilities change (their Figure 1), which is a published statement of the C7 phenomenon; regression-estimator bias negligible in both; rejective variance estimator computed from the initial design performs well on average (cites Fuller 2009a); Deville-Tille 2005 variance estimator matched the initial-design estimator under Poisson (0.120 vs 0.131) but did poorly under stratified initial designs (0.792 vs 0.929) because the Poisson approximation fails in small strata; no confidence-interval coverage reported; no clusters, no predictions. n = 20 and 80 only.

authors: Caren Hasler; Esther Eustache; Yves Tille
title: In Search of the Most Balanced Sampling Design
closeness: medium (balanced designs generally; rejective, rerandomization and cube named as the existing approaches)
what_it_holds: [from abstract only] Finds the design (support plus probabilities) that makes weighted sample totals of auxiliary variables closest to known totals given fixed inclusion probabilities. Exact solution is a linear program over all samples, infeasible beyond tiny populations; proposes a genetic algorithm combining minimum support designs and highly balanced candidate samples. No optimality guarantee; improves balance over cube method. Applies to survey sampling and experimental design. Abstract does not mention clusters or ML predictions. Relevant because G is small (15 to 50) so exhaustive enumeration of C(G,n) samples for n = 4 to 16 may be feasible, which is the regime where an exact balanced design is available.
